items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: And this fellow comes up to me the last night before closing night, he came up and said, “I dig your playing.” ... I went in the next night and there was Charlie Parker, who had said, “I dig your playing, man.”

ctx.x: Well you just said something, it was almost an aside, when you were describing, okay we’re going to play “These Foolish Things” just about here, and, we’re just going to play it for the people, we’re not going to bop it. Now there’s a lot in that statement actually I think. Was bop music, when you’re playing bop, is it more for the musicians than it is for your audience?

Truthfully I never thought of playing, that I was playing bop. I was always a swing player. Sam, coming from this era when he was into the bop era, which was Charlie Parker etcetera, it was a different feeling entirely. I used to play a few figures and say I felt like I was playing bebop there. And he would say, “Yeah there are a couple of things there,” like okay big brother, you almost made it that time. But once in a while I would hear myself back and I’d say two of those bars I thought were a little boppy you…
Sounds good to me. These particular records, I like that title by the way.
